correctness.rationale: For n>=4 the exact graph neighborhoods imply no triangles and at most two common neighbors for nonadjacent pairs. The dual of the ordinary 3-cut complex has the complete one-skeleton, exactly 6n path triangles and n square tetrahedra, and no higher simplex. Straight-triangle free-edge collapses and per-square tetrahedron/triangle collapses leave a Möbius band plus 2n(n-4) independent graph chords, hence wedge of 2n(n-4)+1 circles. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality gives free homology only in degree 2n-4; full (2n-6) skeleton implies simple connectivity, successive Hurewicz and Whitehead yield the claimed wedge homotopy type. The actual standalone package verifier independently checks dual faces and F2 chain ranks for n=4..10, original full face-poset Morse matching acyclicity and integral unit attaching row for n=4..8; finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact ordinary k=3 homotopy classification for every Möbius ladder n>=4 is not supplied by any compared result. The closest comprehensive primary paper arXiv:2304.13675v2 defines ordinary 3-cut and proves conditional skeleton/homology theorems but does not analyze these ladders; Theorem 6.1 requires a full codimension-one skeleton, whereas the present dual has tetrahedra and so that hypothesis fails. The 2026 primary article arXiv:2608.30601v2 determines independence and perfect-matching complexes and explicitly names cut complexes as a future direction in Problem 26. The published-finding corpus Wagner M8 hit describes the distinct total 3-cut complex, not the ordinary one. Search coverage cannot establish priority over unindexed work.
residual_risks: Unindexed or unpublished prior calculations of ordinary three-cut complexes of Möbius ladders might exist.
Abstract-only review of the powers-of-cycles paper leaves unspecified secondary results uninspected; its stated principal family nevertheless differs from Möbius ladders.

value.rationale: This exact all-n integral homotopy type for the first nontrivial ordinary cut parameter on the Möbius ladder family addresses the explicit graph-complex direction in Agarwal--Basak arXiv:2608.30601v2 Problem 26. The Möbius-strip Alexander-dual collapse identifies a robust geometric mechanism for the Betti ranks, not an arbitrary small-parameter table or a mere rephrasing of known independence/perfect-matching results.
